title: Dropdowns and Selects
summary: Selects suit finite option sets; they add interaction cost and hide alternatives.

MUST.text: Use native `<select>` when option count and platform behavior fit; add typeahead/search for long lists.
Provide an accessible name and keyboard operability (native or APG listbox pattern).
Group options with optgroup/headers and sort predictable catalogues.

SHOULD.text: Prefer radios or segmented controls for 2–5 mutually exclusive choices that benefit from scanning (heuristic, not WCAG).
Show loading/empty states and provide a clear option when the field is optional.

AVOID.text: Do not hide 2–5 mutually exclusive choices in a dropdown when radios scan faster (heuristic, not a WCAG criterion).
Do not build a custom select without keyboard, focus and ARIA support.

EXAMPLE.good: Country list uses a searchable select; yes/no uses radios
EXAMPLE.bad: 3 yes/no options hidden in a dropdown

FAILURE_MODES: Custom selects lose keyboard and assistive-tech support.
Hidden options increase selection errors and time.
Unsorted or ungrouped long lists impede scanning.
